chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Barqi, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira and Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Talha ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding this verse:
'And do not turn your cheek away from people [in contempt]'
He said: 'Let the people be equal with you in knowledge.'

key_terms.الْعِلْمُ: Knowledge, especially religious and scholarly knowledge
key_terms.تُصَعِّرْ: To turn one's cheek away in contempt or arrogance (from ṣa'ar, a disease causing animals to tilt their necks)

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq say about sharing knowledge equally with all people?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) interprets Quran 31:18, a verse from Surah Luqman that prohibits arrogant, contemptuous behavior toward others, as a command to share knowledge equally with all people without distinction. The original context of the Quranic verse is Luqman's admonition to his son against pride and haughtiness. The Imam extends this to mean that one who possesses knowledge must not withhold it from others based on their social status or perceived worthiness — all people should have equal access to knowledge.
